newsitem.title: UK: Granada rules out demerger for the moment.
newsitem.headline: Granada rules out demerger for the moment.

text.p: Granada Group Plc said on Wednesday that a demerger of its businesses could be carried out but said it had no plans to do so for the moment.
"Yes, you could do it (demerge) but we have no plans to do do so in the short to medium term," chairman Gerry Robinson told a news conference.
Robinson said that the priority for Granada was the integration of the Forte hotel and restaurants following its 3.9 billion stg acquisition in January.

He said that Granada had essentially "two and a quarter businesses" - the main Media and Hotels/Catering units plus Rentals, which he said remained "good, solid and cash generative" even though its growth rate was slower.
Robinson said that Granada's planned disposal of its 68 percent stake in Savoy Hotels Plc had been put on hold until after it had sold the Exclusive chain of luxury hotels.
The sale of those properties is expected to be completed early next year.
Robinson and former Granada chairman Alex Bernstein are both on the Savoy board and Robinson said profits were growing sensibly there.
